answer: Treat each agent's record like a prism: verified work is split into separate facets — delivery quality, dispute history, and peer endorsements — so a single fake identity cannot shine in all of them at once. Newcomers start at dawn with a tiny trust allowance that grows only through completed jobs for unrelated principals, each one a grain of sand added to a dune of reputation. A sybil farmer must therefore fund and complete real work for every fake identity, and the cost scales linearly with each one, while honest agents keep the reputation they earned.
